message.content:
Host: this Proxmox server (ns5002569), running nginx for Nxeon's live production sites. Real production infrastructure — be careful, this task touches live nginx config for domains with real traffic.

## What's already done

A self-contained, branded "we'll be right back" maintenance page already exists at `/opt/nxeon/public/maintenance.html` — a static HTML file with everything inlined (CSS, an embedded base64 logo, a subtle animated glow-ring effect matching Nxeon's brand, auto-refreshes every 20s via a meta tag). It needs ZERO backend/app dependency to render — it's designed specifically to be served by nginx directly when the Next.js app itself is down, which is exactly the scenario it needs to cover. Do not edit its content/design — that part is finished. Just read it if you want to confirm it exists and looks complete before wiring it in.

## What you need to do

Wire this page into nginx so it's automatically shown to visitors whenever the backend returns 502/503/504 (i.e., whenever the Nxeon app is down/restarting/erroring at the proxy level — exactly what happened today during a real outage, which is why this page was requested).

Nginx site configs live in `/etc/nginx/sites-enabled/`. Relevant ones for Nxeon (there are other unrelated sites in this directory too — e.g. `kodely`, `trynxeon-redirect` — leave those alone, they are a different product/owner):
- `nxeon-cloud` — the primary customer-facing domain (nxeon.cloud), proxies to `127.0.0.1:3000`
- `nxeon` — likely a legacy/secondary Nxeon vhost, check its `server_name` and proxy target before touching it
- `nxeon-admin-cloud` — the admin ops portal (a secret subdomain), proxies to the app
- `nxeon-staging` — staging customer portal
- `nxeon-staging-admin` — staging admin portal

Read each file fully before editing. For each `server { }` block in each file that has a `proxy_pass` to the Nxeon app (skip any block that's just an HTTP->HTTPS redirect or an ACME challenge handler — those have nothing to show a maintenance page for), add:

1. An `error_page 502 503 504 /maintenance.html;` directive inside that server block.
2. A `location = /maintenance.html { root /opt/nxeon/public; internal; }` block (or without `internal` if you determine nginx's default error_page handling needs it reachable — verify by testing, see below). Use the correct static file root for that vhost — staging vhosts might expect a different root path (check whether staging has its own copy of `/opt/nxeon-staging/public/` and mirror the SAME file there via `cp`, or just point staging's location block at the production path `/opt/nxeon/public/maintenance.html` too, whichever is simpler and still correct — the page's content doesn't reference environment-specific URLs so serving the same file from either location is fine, use your judgement for the cleanest wiring given how each vhost's config is structured).

## Critical safety requirements

- **`nginx -t` after every edit, before reloading.** Never reload with a config that hasn't passed `nginx -t`.
- **Reload nginx only via `systemctl reload nginx`** (graceful, does not drop existing connections) — never `restart` (that would cause a real, unnecessary blip on every live site nginx serves, not just Nxeon's).
- After reloading, verify normal traffic is completely unaffected: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://nxeon.cloud/` should still return 200, and the admin/staging equivalents should behave identically to before your change. Do NOT deliberately take down the app to test the 502 page against live production — instead, verify correctness by testing directly against nginx's static file serving (e.g. `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1/maintenance.html` with the right Host header, or by temporarily stopping ONLY the STAGING web service — `systemctl stop nxeon-staging-web`, confirm staging's maintenance page now appears (`curl -s https://<staging-domain>/ | grep -o "We'll be right back"` or similar), then `systemctl start nxeon-staging-web` immediately after and confirm staging is back to normal). Never stop the PRODUCTION `nxeon-web` service to test this — that would cause a real, unnecessary customer-facing outage. Staging is the safe place to prove the mechanism works end-to-end.
- If a vhost's config is more complex than a simple proxy (e.g. has multiple location blocks with different upstream ports, like `nxeon-cloud`'s `/console-ws`/`/terminal-ws` websocket blocks) — the error_page directive at the server-block level applies platform-wide for that server block regardless of which location matched, which is what you want (any upstream failure inside that domain shows the same maintenance page). You don't need one per location block, just one per server block that proxies to the app.

## Verification checklist before you report done

1. `nginx -t` passes with the final config.
2. `systemctl reload nginx` succeeded (check `systemctl status nginx` after).
3. Every Nxeon vhost still serves normal traffic at 200 (spot-check nxeon.cloud and the staging domain — find staging's actual domain from its `server_name` directive in `nxeon-staging`'s config).
4. You proved the maintenance page actually renders when the backend is down, using the staging-stop-and-restart method above (not production).
5. List every file you modified and a one-line diff summary for each.

Report back concisely: what you changed, how you verified it, and confirm current live traffic is unaffected.

content.thinking: I should look through all the relevant nginx config files in full to understand the setup.

Now I have the full picture and I'm identifying which server blocks proxy to the Nxeon app. The nxeon-cloud config has a port 80 redirect block to skip, and a port 443 block for nxeon.cloud proxying to 127.0.0.1:3000 that needs error_page and location directives added; the legacy nxeon config for revsports.ca also has a redirect-only port 80 block to skip.

Continuing through the legacy nxeon file, the revsports.ca port 443 block just redirects to nxeon.cloud so I skip it, but the admin ops portal block on port 443 actually proxies live traffic to 127.0.0.1:3000, so despite being legacy it should get the error_page treatment too. Same goes for the default_server bare-IP block on port 443, and the port 80 default_server block also directly proxies non-ACME paths to the app, so it needs the same fix.

Moving to the other config files: nxeon-admin-cloud has one redirect block to skip and one proxying to 3000 that needs the error_page added. For nxeon-staging, the primary and backward-compat blocks (staging.nxeon.cloud and staging.revsports.ca) both proxy to 3001, as does the direct-IP :8080 fallback, so all three get the fix while the port 80 redirect is skipped. Finally nxeon-staging-admin follows the same pattern -- skip the redirect, add error_page to the port 443 block proxying to 3001.

Now for the maintenance page's root path, I'm checking whether staging's public directory already has a copy of maintenance.html -- it has plenty of other files but not that one. I could point staging's config directly at production's path, but that creates a cross-directory dependency that feels a bit fragile even though it'd technically always work since they're on the same host. I'd rather copy the file into staging's own public directory so its config stays self-contained.

For the `internal;` directive, marking the location internal is exactly right here since it means the location can only be reached via nginx's internal redirect mechanism like error_page, not by direct external requests -- which matches what the task needs.

I'll go with internal as the primary approach, test it, and remove it if it fails to serve properly. Let me proceed with editing each config file, checking nginx -t after all edits, then reloading once — starting with adding the error_page and location block to nxeon-cloud's 443 server block for the customer portal.

## Summary

**Files modified** (all in `/etc/nginx/sites-available/`, symlinked into `sites-enabled/`):

1. **`nxeon-cloud`** — added `error_page 502 503 504 /maintenance.html;` + internal `location = /maintenance.html { root /opt/nxeon/public; }` to the `nxeon.cloud`/`www.nxeon.cloud` HTTPS server block (proxies to `127.0.0.1:3000`). The HTTP→HTTPS redirect block was left untouched.

2. **`nxeon-admin-cloud`** — same directives added to the `4j3d7gkr2wcbi34.nxeon.cloud` HTTPS server block (proxies to `127.0.0.1:3000`), rooted at `/opt/nxeon/public`.

3. **`nxeon`** (legacy revsports.ca vhost) — added the same directives to the three blocks that actually proxy to the app: the old admin subdomain (`4j3d7gkr2wcbi34.revsports.ca`), the default-server 443 bare-IP/self-signed block, and the default-server port-80 block. Left the pure redirect blocks (`revsports.ca` → `nxeon.cloud`, and the HTTP→HTTPS block) untouched.

4. **`nxeon-staging`** — added the directives to all three proxying blocks: `staging.nxeon.cloud` (primary), `staging.revsports.ca` (backward-compat), and the direct-IP `:8080` fallback — all rooted at `/opt/nxeon-staging/public`.

5. **`nxeon-staging-admin`** — added the directives to the `staging.4j3d7gkr2wcbi34.nxeon.cloud` HTTPS block, rooted at `/opt/nxeon-staging/public`.

Also copied `/opt/nxeon/public/maintenance.html` → `/opt/nxeon-staging/public/maintenance.html` (content is environment-agnostic, so staging gets its own local copy rather than depending on the production path).

Left untouched: `kodely` and `trynxeon-redirect` (different product/owner), and `nxeon-mail` (not in the task scope, didn't touch it).

**Verification performed:**
- `nginx -t` passed before and after reload.
- `systemctl reload nginx` (graceful, not `restart`) — confirmed `active (running)`.
- All `location = /maintenance.html` blocks use `internal;` — verified direct external requests to `/maintenance.html` return 404 (not reachable except via nginx's internal error_page redirect).
- Post-reload spot checks: `nxeon.cloud` 200, `www.nxeon.cloud` 200, admin `4j3d7gkr2wcbi34.nxeon.cloud` 302 (unchanged pre-existing redirect-to-/admin behavior), `staging.nxeon.cloud` 200, `staging.4j3d7gkr2wcbi34.nxeon.cloud` 200.
- End-to-end proof: stopped **only** `nxeon-staging-web`, confirmed `https://staging.nxeon.cloud/` returned `502` with the branded maintenance page body (grepped "right back"), then immediately restarted the service and confirmed staging returned to 200. Production `nxeon-web` was never stopped.
